column1: //step The same text | The same text ; One node | Normally the same text always means the same node. This page shows three ways round that.

//step Blank nodes | Blank nodes | A blank node has no name of its own. Write _BN as the subject and give it a type. The lines about _BN that follow all belong to it until another _BN is given a type.
//sub What a blank node is | A blank node ; No name of its own ; The subject _BN ; A line about _BN gives its type ; The _BN lines that follow it ; An automatic number |
//sub An example | _BN-N1 ; Production ; Painting ; London | Here a production is written as a blank node. It has a type and two more lines.
//step Earlier blank nodes | Earlier blank nodes | _BN-1 points to the blank node before the current one and _BN-2 to the one before that. Here the sampling happened after the production.
//step Repeated labels | Repeated labels | Adding #-1 or #-2 to the end of some text makes separate nodes that show the same text. The number is not shown.
//step Class names | Class names | Class names such as crm: names and the word Type get a separate copy for each subject. This stops many links meeting at one node.
